instruction:
Use ANSYS Workbench via the Command Line Interface (CLI) to complete a Steady-State Thermal analysis.

Physical problem:
One-dimensional steady-state heat conduction through a rectangular steel block.

Coordinate system and geometry:
- Use the global Cartesian coordinate system.
- The heat conduction direction is the global X direction.
- The block length is along the X direction.
- The block occupies:
  - 0 ≤ X ≤ 100 mm
  - 0 ≤ Y ≤ 10 mm
  - 0 ≤ Z ≤ 10 mm
- The left end face is the face at X = 0 mm.
- The right end face is the face at X = 100 mm.

Model parameters:
- Block size: 100 mm × 10 mm × 10 mm
- Material: Structural Steel
- Use steady thermal material properties for steel:
  - Thermal conductivity k = 50 W/(m·K)
- Use a consistent unit system in Workbench.
- Use a mesh that includes nodes or elements on the mid-length section at X = 50 mm.

Boundary conditions:
- Left end face at X = 0 mm:
  - Prescribed temperature = 100 °C
- Right end face at X = 100 mm:
  - Prescribed temperature = 20 °C
- All other external faces are adiabatic.

Analysis type:
- Steady-State Thermal analysis.

Save requirements:
- Use C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop as the working location.
- Save the Workbench project file as:
  C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\wb_conduction.wbpj
- Save the MAPDL-equivalent database file as:
  C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\wb_conduction.db
- Save the MAPDL-equivalent thermal result file as:
  C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\wb_conduction.rth
